> ### وصف
> **خطأ في SQLite: فشل قيد NOT NULL: session_message.seq**
> 
> بعد آخر تحديث لـ OpenCode (عمليات الترحيل من 3 إلى 5 يونيو التي أضافت جدول عرض session_message)، تتعطل أي جلسة تُفعّل تبديل الوكيل مع ظهور هذا الخطأ. مسار الكود الخاص بدالة 'ppendMessage()' لـ session.next.agent.switched لا يُوفّر قيمة تسلسلية عند الإدراج في جدول session_message، مع العلم أن العمود مُعرّف كـ INTEGER NOT NULL بدون قيمة افتراضية.
> 
> **تتبع أخطاء النظام:** `SQLiteError: NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq at run (unknown) at #run (bun:sqlite:185:20) at appendMessage (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-j582v44c.js:2:62480) at session.next.agent.switched (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-j582v44c.js:2:56601) at SessionPrompt.createUserMessage (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-rsc45ft5.js:1677:366)`
> 
> **السبب الجذري:** يحتوي مخطط جدول session_message على قيمة تسلسلية من نوع عدد صحيح غير فارغة (NO DEFAULT). عند استدعاء الدالة 'ppendMessage()' أثناء عملية تبديل الوكيل التالي (session.next.agent.switched)، يتم إدراج البيانات في جدول session_message دون تحديد الحقل التسلسلي (seq).
> 
> عمليات الترحيل ذات الصلة:
> 
> * 20260603001617_session_message_projection_indexes
> * 20260603040000_session_message_projection_order
> * 20260603160727_jittery_ezekiel_stane
> 
> **شهادة:**
> 
> * يحتوي جدول session_message على 0 صفوف (كل عملية إدخال تفشل)
> * يحتوي جدول الرسائل القديم على أكثر من 680 صفًا (لا يزال النظام القديم يعمل)
> * يحدث الخطأ فقط على مسار session.next.agent.switched
> * عمود التسلسل لا يحتوي على قيمة فارغة ولكن ليس له قيمة افتراضية
> 
> **الحل البديل:** `sql ALTER TABLE session_message RENAME TO session_message_old; CREATE TABLE session_message ( id text PRIMARY KEY, session_id text NOT NULL, type text NOT NULL, time_created integer NOT NULL, time_updated integer NOT NULL, data text NOT NULL, seq integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, CONSTRAINT fk_session_message_session_id_session_id_fk FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES session(id) ON DELETE CASCADE ); INSERT INTO session_message SELECT * FROM session_message_old; DROP TABLE session_message_old; `
> 
> ### الإضافات
> oh-my-openagent, opencode-agent-skills, aegis
> 
> ### إصدار مفتوح المصدر
> الإصدار الأخير (تم تحديثه تلقائيًا في 6 يونيو 2026 تقريبًا)
> 
> ### خطوات إعادة الإنتاج
> 1. تشغيل OpenCode باستخدام إضافة oh-my-openagent (سلوك تبديل الوكيل)
> 2. تشغيل سير عمل يؤدي إلى تبديل الوكيل التالي في الجلسة
> 3. لاحظ الخطأ: فشل قيد NOT NULL: session_message.seq
>

I’m seeing another failure mode that appears to be related to the same Muse Spark / OpenCode Zen problem described here.

My setup is OpenCode Desktop on Windows using the built-in `opencode` provider. I am not using Muse through an external API, proxy, or third-party integration.

For me, the problem started around four days ago and was initially rare, but it has become more frequent.

The important detail is that it is **intermittent**:

* `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free, muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free` sometimes works normally.
* At other times it fails, including in completely new sessions.
* I have also seen the same behavior with `muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free`.
* Other free models continue to work normally in the exact same OpenCode Desktop installation and environment.

The error I am currently getting is:

```text
Error from provider (Console): Upstream request failed:
[invalid_request_error] reasoning `encrypted_content` was not issued to this caller
```

I have already updated OpenCode Desktop to the latest version available to me, but the problem remains.

This does not look like a normal corrupted-session problem from my side, because creating a new session does not reliably resolve it. The fact that other free models work normally is also significant.

This seems especially interesting in light of the existing report here, which already shows intermittent failures specifically affecting Muse Spark 1.2/1.3 through the OpenCode provider, including failures in brand-new sessions while another free model works correctly:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/47237

There is also a separate recent report showing the **exact same `encrypted_content` error** with `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` through OpenCode Zen:

https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/11928

That report is particularly interesting because the error is coming from the upstream provider and is explicitly associated with `opencode-zen` + `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`.

OpenCode's Zen documentation also shows that Muse Spark uses the Responses API path:

https://opencode.ai/docs/zen

So I’m wondering whether there may currently be an intermittent issue in the Zen → Muse Spark reasoning state / `encrypted_content` handling, possibly in addition to the `Invalid upload request` issue reported here.

I don't want to jump to a conclusion about the exact root cause, but the pattern is now quite consistent from my side:

**same Desktop + same account + same environment → other free models work → Muse Spark 1.2/1.3 intermittently fail → fresh sessions do not reliably fix it.**

Hopefully adding this case helps correlate the different Muse Spark failures on the backend. I’m happy to provide timestamps, session IDs, or OpenCode logs if those would help trace the affected requests.

For anyone still hitting this issue, I tested the fix in @1837620622's [fork](https://github.com/1837620622/opencode) and it worked for me.

The fix is on branch `fix/stale-encrypted-reasoning` at `87dd316b3fdd8abe2b11b4e4d6594aedc7fba818` (fork `dev` does NOT contain the fix, it's the parent of the fix. Checkout the fix branch, not `dev`).

OpenAI-Responses `invalid_encrypted_content` / `encrypted_content was not issued to this caller` stale-reasoning replay. This patch adds a `stale-reasoning` classification and a `ContinueAfterStaleReasoning` single-retry that strips the stale `reasoning.encrypted_content` + `itemId` and retries once.

I can't attach a prebuilt binary (don't run a random binary you can't inspect), so build from source. You'll need bun `^1.3.14` (pinned in `packageManager`, I used 1.4.2):

```bash
# clone the patched fork
git clone https://github.com/1837620622/opencode.git
cd opencode

# checkout the fix branch (not dev)
git checkout fix/stale-encrypted-reasoning
# pinned hash if you want it: 87dd316b3fdd8abe2b11b4e4d6594aedc7fba818

bun install && bun dev
# bun dev = bun run --cwd packages/opencode src/index.ts, same CLI as the binary
```

To build your own patched binary (single-platform):

```bash
./packages/opencode/script/build.ts --single
```
*The `--single` flag builds only for the current platform. Without it the script builds the full 12-target matrix (linux/darwin/windows x arm64/x64 x baseline/musl).*

Install side-by-side so you can run from anywhere:

```bash
./install --binary ./packages/opencode/dist/opencode-darwin-arm64/bin/opencode
```

You can add a `localcode` function in your rc if you want running to be seamless:

```bash
# Runs the local patched build from anywhere. No args = current directory.
localcode() {
  local bin="$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode"
  if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    "$bin" .
  else
    "$bin" "$@"
  fi
}
```

Or symlink if you prefer: `ln -sf ~/.opencode/bin/opencode ~/.local/bin/localcode`

+1 here. This bug also affects opencode sessions with MiniMax-M3 (Anthropic-compatible endpoint) — confirmed empirically in our setup. Sessions accumulate `cache_read` tokens to multi-billion levels without ever triggering compaction, then hit context overflow on the next API call. The PR #46136 fix using cumulative tokens looks correct and tests pass — would really appreciate a review/merge on this one. Tracking in our internal config (`compaction.reserved: 500000`) doesn't help because `isOverflow` only looks at the last message, not the accumulated context. Workaround: manual `/compact` every 20-30 messages until this lands.

2. **Configured provider timeouts do not reach this layer.** The desktop bundle contains no `headersTimeout`/`bodyTimeout`/`Dispatcher` configuration; the SDK's caller-side `timeout`/`AbortSignal` options are cancellation only. So a user who configures, e.g., a 3 000 s provider request timeout still dies at ~302 s — the configured wait budget never applies to the headers phase of the non-streaming `session.prompt` RPC (whose headers arrive only at turn completion).

3. **A new failure class: multi-call agentic turns die mid-turn, not just single slow calls.** In our environment a 150-call agentic task (wall time 5–19 min depending on concurrent load — the server's decode rate is 200+ tok/s; the variance is admission queuing) dies at ~302 s with only a small fraction of the work committed, and the driver's retry re-scans the whole scope. Same `HeadersTimeoutError` signature, but it turns a long-but-successful run into a partial-failure loop.

For reference, the stopgap we filed on the Magic Context side (per-category task scoping so runs fit the window as it exists today) is cortexkit/magic-context#451. The durable fix remains applying a configurable/extended undici headers+body timeout in the SDK dispatcher, as #33535 attempted.

I investigated this at the OS level and confirmed that this is inotify watch exhaustion, not disk exhaustion.

Diagnostics while the issue was active:

```
$ df -h /
/dev/nvme0n1p2  938G  206G  684G  24% /

$ df -i /
/dev/nvme0n1p2  60M  3.6M  57M  6% /

$ sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_watches
fs.inotify.max_user_watches = 524288
```

Counting inotify descriptors and watch entries under `/proc/*/fdinfo` showed:

```
TOTAL instances=24 watches=524250
524202 watches  3 instances  opencode2 serve --service
```

One inotify FD owned by the existing OpenCode service contained **524,129 watches** by itself. The service command was:

```
.../.opencode2-wrapped serve --service
```

There was only one OpenCode service plus its client wrapper running. Launching a second `opencode2` TUI then reproduced the crash exactly:

```
ENOSPC: no space left on device, watch '/home/capcu/.local/state/opencode/beta/tui'
at new FSWatcher (internal:fs/watch:101:31)
```

The system journal also showed unrelated processes (systemd user services, Chromium, tmux scopes, GNOME Keyring) failing to add inotify watches with `No space left on device`, confirming that OpenCode had exhausted the user-wide kernel watch pool.

So the likely failure mode is that the long-running Bun-based OpenCode service accumulates/leaks recursive filesystem watches until it reaches `fs.inotify.max_user_watches`. The next OpenCode instance is merely where the exhausted limit becomes visible. Restarting the service releases those watches, which explains why that temporarily fixes it.

Environment: OpenCode `0.0.0-beta-19271`, Linux 6.18.44 x64, system Bun `1.3.13` (though OpenCode's embedded Bun version may differ).

### End-to-end proof via AGENT_TRACE_TABLE

Ran two requests against a live AI gateway (`openai-gpt-5.4` via `DEFAULT_GATEWAY`), then queried `TABLE(AGENT_TRACE_TABLE('DEFAULT_GATEWAY'))`:

**Test 1 (no traceparent):** gateway server span gets its own trace_id, disconnected from any client trace.

**Test 2 (with traceparent `00-e2bc2acd...-620bb0e5...-01`):** gateway server span adopts the client trace context:

```
trace=e2bc2acd791b48ff  span=620bb0e5fee04c14  parent=(root)           SPAN_KIND_CLIENT  opencode.chat.completions
trace=e2bc2acd791b48ff  span=e036e58baf3757f2  parent=620bb0e5fee04c14  SPAN_KIND_SERVER  chat openai-gpt-5.4
```

The server span's `parent_span_id` (`620bb0e5fee04c14`) matches the client span_id from the `traceparent` header. Both spans share the same `trace_id`. This is a single connected distributed trace.

Without the traceparent header, the gateway's server spans start independent traces with no link back to the client. The PR fix (`propagation.inject()` in `executor.ts`) adds this header when OTel tracing is configured.

Addressed all three findings in 1fcafcb (pushed to this branch):

**P1 — malformed config wedging reload.** Verified the premise: `ConfigParse.jsonc` throws, which surfaces through the cached `loadGlobal` as a defect that `orElseSucceed` doesn't cover, and my original ordering read `getGlobal()` before `invalidate()`. The gate now reads via `catchCause` (covers defects, logs a warning), always runs `invalidate()`, and treats an unreadable config as *changed* — the previous unconditional-dispose behavior — so a bad file can neither skip invalidation nor pin the cache. `global-lifecycle.test.ts` covers failure → disposal with invalidation, then normal gating after the file is fixed.

**P2 — project/custom config inputs.** The gate now covers per-instance inputs, not just the global config. `ConfigFingerprint.hashInstanceInputs(directory, worktree)` hashes exactly what the instance loader reads from disk: the project `opencode.json/jsonc` chain, every config directory's agent/mode/command/plugin files (mirroring the loader, including its `.opencode` filter for the json files), and the `OPENCODE_CONFIG` override. `InstanceStore` captures the fingerprint at boot and exposes `configChanged()`, which re-hashes loaded instances and reports drift; a missing or unreadable baseline counts as changed. Theme files are deliberately excluded — they're rendering-only, and are what the signal is actually about. Covered by a `configChanged` integration test in `instance.test.ts` and unit tests in `fingerprint.test.ts`.

**P2 — key reorder false positive.** Config comparison now uses `canonicalEquals` (order-insensitive structural equality), and the fingerprint canonicalizes parsed JSON before hashing, so pure key reordering no longer disposes or registers as drift. Both levels have tests.

One related note: #42622 (defer disposal until sessions idle) is a complementary approach — this PR gates *whether* to dispose, that one would gate *when*. If both land, the gate here still avoids needless rebuilds for theme-only signals.

Verification: `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun test test/server test/config test/project` → 629 pass, 0 fail; oxlint clean on touched files.
